record.field: Odoo was originally called TinyERP when founded in 2005 by Fabien Pinckaers in Belgium.
history
The name "Odoo" was chosen in 2014 and is meant to sound friendly and approachable!
history
Odoo S.A. is headquartered in Grand-Rosière, Belgium - a small village with big software ambitions!
history
Odoo has over 12 million users worldwide and is used in 120+ countries.
history
The OWL framework (Odoo Web Library) powers all modern Odoo frontend components - including this chess game!
feature
Odoo's longpolling bus allows real-time updates without page refreshes - that's how you see your opponent's moves instantly!
feature
Odoo has 82+ official apps and over 50,000 community apps on the Odoo App Store!
feature
The mail.thread mixin provides automatic activity tracking - that's why game invitations show up in your activities!
feature
Odoo's ORM supports computed fields with dependencies - like how the current player is automatically calculated from the FEN position!
feature
Pro tip: Use Ctrl+K anywhere in Odoo to open the command palette for quick navigation!
tip
Did you know? You can click on most field labels in Odoo forms to access field-specific actions!
tip
Odoo tip: Use the "/" key in text fields to access quick formatting and block insertion options!
tip
Press "?" in most Odoo views to see available keyboard shortcuts for that view!
tip
The Odoo mascot is an elephant named "Odie" - because elephants never forget your data!
fun
Odoo Experience is the largest annual business software conference in Europe, held in Brussels!
fun
The Odoo Community Association (OCA) has contributed over 2,500 modules to the Odoo ecosystem!
fun
Odoo's purple color (#714B67) is actually called "Odoo Purple" and represents creativity and innovation!
fun
While you're playing chess, somewhere an Odoo developer is probably fixing a bug - or creating a new feature!
fun
This chess game uses python-chess for move validation - the same library used by Lichess and chess.com!
fun
The FEN notation storing your game position was invented in 1883 - older than most ERP systems!
fun
The Elo rating system used here was created by Arpad Elo in 1960 for the US Chess Federation.
